rationale: Evidence from tool calls shows the agent authenticated the user and acted on order #W5270061, looked up relevant products, and executed a write to modify two items using a gift card payment method. However, there is no evidence of explicit user confirmation prior to the order-changing write, which policy requires. The user also requested a shipping address change; instead of completing it, the agent modified items first and then transferred to a human citing a restriction, leaving the address change unresolved. While handoff is appropriate when the agent cannot proceed, the sequence created a dependency that blocked the address update and the request was not completed. Therefore, the interaction does not meet the pass bar (missing confirmation before write and incomplete fulfillment of the user’s request).
